Staged Acceptance Scheduler and Grace-Level Degradation for Regional Failover

Problem statement:
During regional failovers and transient overloads we currently rely on coarse-grained token-bucket based shedding and model-variant fallbacks. This has led to oscillation (clients repeatedly retried between regions) and poor tail-latency SLOs for higher-priority tenants. We need a more deterministic admission approach that: 1) preserves strong SLOs for tenant service classes, 2) reduces oscillatory retry behavior across regions, and 3) provides clear, measurable graceful-degradation levels that can be observed and tuned over time.

Goal:
Introduce a Staged Acceptance Scheduler (SAS) that combines staged admission windows, deferred-acceptance slots, and explicit grace-level degradation modes to enable predictable, multi-region failover and admission control. SAS should integrate with the existing routing/fallback layers and provide operator-visible metrics and controls for per-tenant SLAs and global SLO enforcement.

User stories:
- As a platform SRE, I want high-priority tenants to maintain latency SLOs during regional spikes, while lower-priority tenants accept degraded fidelity rather than hard failures.
- As an engineering owner, I want deterministic, observable rules that prevent cross-region retry storms during failover.
- As an operator, I want a knob to incrementally move traffic through staged acceptance windows to validate health before full failover cutover.
- Staged Acceptance Scheduler implemented in admission controller runtime with configuration flags.
- Three grace-level modes available: full-fidelity, reduced-fidelity (token trimming / model-slimming), deferred-acceptance (delayed enqueue up to X ms then reject).
- Per-tenant service_class mapping honored; high class requests prioritized into higher acceptance bands.
- Multi-region failover flow uses staged acceptance windows to gradually onboard traffic to the healthy region with health checks gating each stage.
- Observability: per-stage accepted/rejected counters, latency percentiles, retry-loop detection metric, and SLO impact dashboard.
- Integration tests and chaos tests covering region cutover and spike scenarios.
- Rollout plan validated in canary -> blue/green -> fleet rollout with feature flag gating.
Design alternatives considered:
1) Keep existing token-buckets + static priority bands (rejected due to oscillation during region handoff).
2) Full request queuing with long tail latencies (rejected; violates P99 SLOs for high-priority tenants).
3) Staged Acceptance Scheduler (selected): admission is split into short, explicit windows (Stage 0..N). Each stage has configurable capacity and grace mode. Gate transitions on health signals and p99 latency targets.

Key decisions:
- Use 4-stage default pipeline: Probe (small sample), Warm (gradual ramp), Ramp (majority), Open (full).
- Introduce 'deferred-acceptance' that enqueues low-priority requests into a soft reservoir for up to 200ms before final decision; reservoir size proportional to tenant weight.
- Implement grace-modes as composable handlers: fidelity-trim, response-stream-skip, compact-embedding-mode. These are policy-bound and pluggable per model family.
- Backpressure propagation: admission controller returns structured feedback headers to clients indicating stage and recommended retry/backoff. This reduces blind retries across regions.

Architecture notes:
- Admission controller: new module in the frontend API layer responsible for stage assignment and per-request policy enforcement.
- Stage controller: central coordinator that advances stages based on cluster health signals (region heartbeats, model-serving latency p99, queue depth).
- Telemetry: per-tenant/time-bucketed counters emitted to metrics pipeline (Prometheus + ClickHouse downstream).
- Config: feature-flag controlled with rollout percentage and per-tenant overrides in config DB.
Phase 0 (Spike/prototype): implement SAS prototype behind feature flag on canary region (done).
Phase 1 (Canary): enable SAS-Stage 0/1 for < 5% traffic on US-WEST for low-risk tenants. Monitor metrics for 48h.
Phase 2 (Gradual): expand to 20% traffic and enable deferred-acceptance for P3 tenants only. Observe retry-loop metric and cross-region egress.
Phase 3 (Regional failover drills): run controlled failover drills gating stage progression with synthetic traffic.
Phase 4 (Full): enable on all regions for configured tenant cohorts; expose operator controls in Console.
Rollback: feature flag kill switch; immediate fallback to token-bucket-only admission.
Communication: runbook and on-call playbook updates; announce to customer success for enterprise tenants with dedicated capacity.
Primary metrics:
- stage.accepted.count (labels: region, tenant, stage)
- stage.rejected.count (labels: reason, tenant)
- deferred.reservoir.queued_ms_p90
- per-tenant.p99_latency_ms (pre/post stage)
- retry_loop_count (requests that retried across regions within 30s)
- SLO_breach_rate (tenants with > threshold p99 breaches)

SLO/alert thresholds:
- If high-class tenants see >1% increase in p99 vs baseline for 15m -> alert paging.
- If retry_loop_count increases > 50% baseline for 10m -> alert and throttle stage progression.
- If deferred.reservoir.queued_ms_p90 > 250ms -> auto-reduce deferred reservoir size.
Unit tests for stage assignment logic and policy evaluation.
E2E tests with synthetic traffic generator simulating regional failover + gradual ramp.
Chaos tests: kill region agent, simulate model-serving p99 spike, validate that stage controller pauses and prevents Open stage.
Load tests: ensure SAS adds < 2% overhead on frontend CPU under typical traffic.
Canary observability: pre-defined dashboards and alert burn-in period of 72h before broad rollout.
Risk: deferred-acceptance can increase tail latency for low-priority tenants -> Mitigation: hard upper bound on reservoir wait and aggressive fallback to reject.
Risk: misconfiguration leads to under-acceptance for critical tenants -> Mitigation: require explicit per-tenant overrides for P0/P1 and provide preflight checks.
Risk: clients don't respect structured feedback headers and keep retrying across regions -> Mitigation: add retry-loop detector and tenant-specific circuit-breaker that enforces a cooldown on re-entrance.
Risk: increased complexity in the admission path -> Mitigation: keep core admission path fast-path (Stage Open) and only add processing for staged/deferred paths.

2026-02-22 Aisha Patel: Spike completed. Prototype can accept/reject with stage metadata. Initial perf overhead ~0.9% on canary frontends.
2026-02-26 Marcus Chen: Implemented deferred reservoir with configurable max_wait_ms=200. Added unit tests and basic metrics emission. Opened PR #1892.
2026-03-01 Lucía Ramirez (PM): Reviewed behaviour matrix. Requested that P0 tenants bypass deferred acceptance unless explicitly throttled by operator. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-04 Oliver Grant (SRE): Observability hooks look good. Recommend adding retry_loop_count alert tied to automatic stage rollback. Filed ENG-762999 for auto-rollbacks (dependent).
2026-03-09 Marcus Chen: Canary run (US-WEST) at 5% traffic for 72h. Observed 18% reduction in retry_loop_count and p99 for P1 tenants improved by ~12ms. Some P3 tenants saw deferred queue p90=220ms; tuned reservoir sizing down 20%.
2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Moving to Gradual phase. Need to coordinate with Console team to expose per-tenant stage overrides before broad rollout. Added dependency ENG-772001 (console-feature-flags).
